answer: Because the harbor fee is applied at the ivory exit, the island audit totals the burn and the ledger shows exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys as a result bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never forfeits. Withdrawing stake costs a 2% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 11 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
